title: How Much Does a Fitted Kitchen Cost UK? A Guide
description: How much does a fitted kitchen cost UK homeowners? Compare units, worktops, appliances, fitting and extras with realistic budget ranges and saving tips.
keywords: how much does a new kitchen cost
targetKeyword: how much does a fitted kitchen cost uk

blocks.text: If you are searching for how much a fitted kitchen costs in the UK, the honest answer is that the total depends on far more than the price of the cabinets. As a rough UK guide, a small, straightforward replacement kitchen may typically cost around £8,000 to £12,000, while a larger kitchen with higher-specification units, new appliances and structural or service changes may reach £20,000 to £35,000 or more. Every project differs: room size, specification, access, location and the amount of building work will affect the final price. Get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
Typical total cost of a fitted kitchen in the UK

For a standard kitchen replacement, it helps to think about the project in five main parts: units, worktops, appliances, installation and extras. As a rough UK guide, a budget kitchen with basic laminate worktops and a modest appliance package may typically fall in the £8,000–£12,000 range. A mid-range fitted kitchen may be around £12,000–£20,000, while a larger or more bespoke project can exceed £25,000. Labour and building work can make a substantial difference, particularly if the layout is changing. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

items: Budget kitchen: as a rough UK guide, typically £8,000–£12,000, often with standard units, laminate worktops and carefully selected appliances.
Mid-range kitchen: as a rough UK guide, typically £12,000–£20,000, with more choice of finishes, improved worktops and a broader appliance specification.
Higher-specification kitchen: as a rough UK guide, typically £20,000–£35,000 or more, particularly where there are bespoke units, premium materials, layout changes or substantial renovation work.

What do the units and worktops cost?

The cost of kitchen units varies with the number of cabinets, construction, finish and storage options. As a rough UK guide, standard flat-pack or entry-level units for a small or average-sized kitchen may typically cost around £2,000–£5,000. Mid-range rigid or made-to-measure options may be closer to £5,000–£10,000, while painted, solid timber or highly bespoke cabinetry can cost more. Drawers, tall larders, pull-out storage, integrated bins and internal organisers can increase the price. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

As a rough UK guide, basic laminate worktops in a typical kitchen may typically cost around £500–£1,500. Solid timber, compact laminate, granite, quartz and other stone surfaces may take the worktop budget to £2,000–£5,000 or more, depending on the material, thickness, joins, cut-outs and installation. An undermount sink or detailed edge profile may also add fabrication costs. Choosing a durable laminate or compact laminate can reduce the initial spend without changing the layout. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

Appliance costs vary by brand, model, energy features and whether appliances are integrated. As a rough UK guide, a basic package of an oven, hob, extractor, dishwasher, fridge-freezer and washing machine may typically cost around £2,000–£4,000. Mid-range appliances may take this to £4,000–£7,000, while premium or fully integrated models can cost considerably more. Check whether delivery, removal of old appliances, connection and installation are included, as these may not be covered by a retailer’s headline price. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

As a rough UK guide, installation for a straightforward kitchen may typically cost around £2,000–£5,000, but there is no single standard fitting price. The figure depends on the number of units, worktop material, flooring, tiling, plumbing, electrical work and how ready the room is. Common extras that affect the final price

The difference between an online kitchen price and the final fitted cost can often be the list of extras. Before comparing quotes, ask each contractor to identify these separately so you can see what is included.

items: Removal and disposal of the old kitchen: as a rough UK guide, typically around £300–£800, depending on the amount of cabinetry and waste.
Plumbing and electrical alterations: minor changes may cost several hundred pounds, while relocating or upgrading services can cost more.
Wall preparation, plastering and decorating: as a rough UK guide, typically around £500–£2,000, depending on the condition of the room.
Tiling or splashbacks: as a rough UK guide, typically around £500–£2,500, depending on the area, tile choice and preparation required.
Flooring: as a rough UK guide, typically around £800–£3,000 for many kitchens, with material, subfloor condition and room size affecting the figure.
Structural changes, such as removing a wall or creating a wider opening, can add several thousand pounds and should be assessed separately.
Design fees, delivery, appliance installation, lighting, handles, taps, sinks and waste removal may be included or charged as separate line items.
Every project differs, so use these figures only as a guide and get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

blocks.text: How to reduce the cost without compromising the result

items: Keep the existing layout where possible. Retaining the sink, cooker and dishwasher positions can reduce plumbing, electrical and flooring work.
Spend selectively on visible or heavily used elements. A better worktop and reliable oven may offer more practical value than premium internal accessories in every cabinet.
Compare the complete specification, not just the cabinet price. A low headline figure may exclude fitting, handles, panels, end finishes, delivery or appliance connections.
Use standard cabinet sizes and limit bespoke units to awkward corners or specific storage needs.
Choose a hard-wearing mid-range worktop and a simple splashback if the budget is tight; these can be upgraded later more easily than hidden services.
Ask whether your existing appliances can be reused, but check their dimensions, condition and warranty before designing around them.
Set aside a contingency within your budget for unforeseen work. Older properties can reveal uneven walls, damaged flooring or outdated services once the room is opened up.

blocks.text: What should a fitted kitchen quote include?

A useful quote should describe the units, doors, handles, panels, plinths, worktops, sink, taps and appliances by model or specification. It should also state the labour included, preparation work, removal of the old kitchen, waste disposal, delivery, connections, tiling, flooring and decorating. Ask whether prices include VAT, and confirm how changes or unforeseen work will be agreed. Getting two or three like-for-like quotations can make comparisons more meaningful than choosing the lowest total alone. faq.q: Is it cheaper to buy a kitchen from a retailer or use a local fitter?
